summary: legal checked in 3 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for SearchWoot public beta or full launch; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Decision: keep the service private, keep rights outreach unsent, and do not monetize or publicly display upstream deal data until authoritative rights evidence, human counsel review, security, accuracy, measurement, and owner gates are complete. Evidence: Woot documentation establishes API access but not redistribution, caching, derivatives, alerts, affiliate, advertising, image, price, or trademark rights; current public terms restrict commercial/public data use. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 pass, 20 fail, 6 unknown, with open banner, consent, GA4, privacy, and terms findings. Analytics is configured for the measured fleet, but configuration does not establish lawful consent or disclosure. Amazon evidence is limited to 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission under an unattributed provider row; do not claim site revenue, ROI, margin, or causal lift. Permit only reversible work that adds no new data collection, credentials, permissions, dependencies, cross-site behavior, or public exposure.

SearchWoot data-use review: Woot API deal and price-history data — blocked; missing current commercial/public-display permission, field-level provenance, permitted retention/cache/derivative/display/alert terms, attribution, freshness, correction, and takedown rules. Smallest next action: attach the authoritative terms or written permission record; until then keep the gate private. User alert rules and sync results — evidence_needed; missing data inventory, retention/deletion/correction workflow, processor terms, notification consent, unsubscribe behavior, and access controls. Smallest next action: produce a read-only data-flow and retention table from the repository and deployed configuration. GA4 analytics — evidence_needed; missing deployed consent and withdrawal evidence, GA4 property/data-sharing settings, retention settings, vendor disclosure, and jurisdiction-specific review. Smallest next action: capture existing consent/configuration evidence without enabling tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data — evidence_needed; missing log-field inventory, retention/access controls, vendor terms or DPA review, and incident/data-request procedures. Smallest next action: produce a read-only operator/vendor inventory and flag counsel-required gaps. No item is clear; none is closed.

Launch-readiness progress: the existing four legal tasks remain open; no task is closed because completion evidence is absent. Source-rights evidence is partially complete and supports a blocked disposition. Data-flow evidence is partial from backend/api/main.py, backend/services/fetcher.py, and config.yml, but operator-confirmed retention, deletion, correction, access, and notification records are missing. Consent evidence is partial from privacy.html and cookie-policy.html; GA4 settings and jurisdiction review are missing. Public terms are draft-only and do not establish upstream permission. Next evidence action: attach one dated read-only bundle to the existing checklist containing the repository/config data-flow table, log/vendor inventory, deployed consent capture, GA4 settings, and the rights/field matrix; do not send outreach, change the private gate, enable tracking, or request duplicate telemetry.
